text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGE: gpu-serving-prod is experiencing sustained queue growth; autoscaler not reacting — observed since ~10:02 UTC. Severity: Sev2. Paging oncall.
alex.sre: I’m on it. seeing queue length keep climbing on ml-queue/gpu (avg wait > 45s). thanks for the page.
maria-rt: I can help with metrics. Prometheus shows scrape lag to prometheus-adapter starting ~09:58 UTC, backlog in the adapter queue.
raj-infra: tagging in infra — possible prom-adapter OOM / connector issue again? last time was the adapter hitting 100% CPU when remote write backed up.
alex.sre: quick check: `kubectl get hpa -n inference` shows HPA for gpu-workers stuck at desired: 20, current: 20, max: 60, but pods pending scheduling/insufficient resources.
alex.sre: `kubectl get pods -n inference -w` shows many pods in Pending with reason: `0/12 nodes are available: 12 Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu`
tara-support: Customer impact: support dashboard shows spike in latency for customers using realtime endpoints — some 429/503 reports starting ~10:05 UTC. P1 customers flagged.
maria-rt: digging metrics: prometheus scrape_latency_seconds for prometheus-adapter spiked from 0.2s to 25s at 09:58. Adapter export queue length: 22k. adapter logs: ```ERROR adapter: push failed: context deadline exceeded```
eng-runtime: Q: are we seeing autoscaler callouts failing because custom metrics are stale? If adapter can’t supply metrics, HPA won’t scale.
alex.sre: correct — HPA uses custom metrics from prometheus-adapter. If adapter hasn't returned updated metrics, desired replicas calculation stays flat.
raj-infra: mitigation plan attempt 1: restart prometheus-adapter deployment to clear backlog. I'll patch replicaCount=3 -> `kubectl rollout restart deployment/prometheus-adapter -n monitoring`
alex.sre: doing an emergency manual scale to dedicated GPU pool as mitigation v0: `kubectl scale deployment gpu-emergency --replicas=10 -n inference` to serve immediate load while autoscale heals. This uses reserved-dedicated nodes with spare GPUs.
maria-rt: FYI logs from adapter after restart: ```WARN adapter: starting backfill consumer; processing 22000 queued items```
pagerduty-bot: Acknowledged. On-call escalation: primary -> alex.sre, secondary -> raj-infra.
alex.sre: after manual scale, queue drop observed from 1800 -> 600 in 3m, tail latency improving but still high for some requests.
tara-support: Notifying affected customers: posting status update draft to status.redwood.ai: "We are experiencing degraded inference for some realtime GPU-backed endpoints due to autoscaling delays. Working on mitigation." Should I send now?
eng-runtime: Wait — before public notice, confirm mitigation holding. We should also enable fallback model variant (cpu-serve-safe) for non-critical traffic to reduce GPU pressure. How to flip?
raj-infra: We have route policy `route-fallback: gpu->cpu` can be toggled via console or `curl -X POST https://controlplane/api/v1/routes/fallback` (internal). I’ll run to reduce pressure by offloading batch jobs.
maria-rt: adapter backfill still processing but rate limited. CPU at 80% across adapter pods. I see sporadic 502s to metrics-server from adapter: ```level=error msg="failed to query metrics-server: context deadline exceeded"```
alex.sre: hypothesis: metrics-server also overloaded; HPA cannot get node metrics and combined with stale custom metrics prevents scale out. Let's restart metrics-server after adapter stabilizes. raj?
raj-infra: will restart metrics-server after adapter queue < 2k. Setting an alert on adapter.queue < 2000 to coordinate.
eng-runtime: also consider temporarily raising HPA policy to allow burst scaling bypassing custom metrics: set `behavior.scaleUp.stabilizationWindowSeconds` to 0 and `maxReplicas` to 80. That buys time but risky.
alex.sre: I’m going to bump maxReplicas to 80 for gpu-workers now to allow k8s to scale if nodes exist: `kubectl patch hpa gpu-workers -n inference -p '{"spec": {"maxReplicas": 80}}'`
maria-rt: after HPA patch, HPA desired jumped to 60 then attempted to reach 80 but stuck due to Insufficient GPU nodes. Node autoscaler didn’t kick because cluster autoscaler uses node pools with quota limits.
raj-infra: hitting cloud provider quota for GPUs in us-west-2 on reserved pools. I’m requesting emergency quota increase but that usually takes ~30-60min.
tara-support: Customers on realtime plans seeing improvement after manual scale; updating status page now.
eng-runtime: alternate mitigation: reduce per-request gpu memory by forcing model to smaller variant and lower `max_batch_size` to decrease memory per replica so scheduling can place more pods on existing nodes. Anyone with quick rollout script?
alex.sre: I have a canary patch to runtime config: `--max-batch-size=8` pushed to canary. If canary good, will flip to prod config.
raj-infra: can also create a temporary K8s taint-toleration to allow pods onto preemptible GPU nodes. Risk: preemptions. Might be acceptable for lower-tier traffic.
maria-rt: adapter queue now 1.8k and processing rate catching up. metrics-server restart scheduled in 2m.
eng-runtime: confirm: when metrics-server back, HPA should see node metrics and combined with adapter catch-up we should get autoscaling back to normal.
raj-infra: metrics-server restarted. logs: `metrics-server: started` `kubelet: metric read success`
alex.sre: HPA now shows desired 70 -> scaling events seen: `Scaled up replicaSet/gpu-workers from 20 to 40`
maria-rt: queue trending down to ~120 after scale. Latency returning to baseline for most customers.
tara-support: Sent update to customers at 10:38 UTC. No new 5xx reports after scale.
eng-runtime: we should keep emergency maxReplicas=80 for another 15m, then revert to normal after cluster capacity confirmed. Also need a post-incident action: improve adapter backpressure handling and make prometheus-adapter autoscale earlier.
raj-infra: opening infra follow-up ticket: `INFRA-4372` notes: cloud GPU quota automation, node pool burst policy, and preemptible fallback.
alex.sre: opening incident postmortem ticket: `INC-2026` capturing timeline, mitigation steps, customer impact.
maria-rt: logs and metrics snapshots saved to `/incidents/2987654321/artifacts/` (internal).
incident-bot: Incident status: mitigated -> partial; monitoring for 30m before declaring resolved.
alex.sre: thanks team. handoff to night oncall in 40m: @raj-infra will be primary then.
raj-infra: acknowledged. I’ll pick up.
tara-support: closing urgent customer notifications, will follow up with affected accounts individually.
eng-runtime: follow-ups: (1) adapter autoscale tuning, (2) metrics-server HA review, (3) HPA fallback policy + synthetic metrics to guard against adapter blackhole.
alex.sre: closing notes: root cause - prometheus-adapter backlog + metrics-server spikiness -> HPA blind -> queue growth + GPU capacity limits + cloud quota hit blocked autoscale. Recovery via manual scale + adapter restart + metrics-server restart + temporary HPA max bump + route fallback and model config tuning.
incident-bot: Incident moved to status: monitoring. If no regressions, will mark resolved in 30m. :white_check_mark:
